The apparatus comprises: a first sensing unit configured to acquire a first position signal indicative of the position of a first element placed at a location on the surface of the body that undergoes the surface motion; a second sensing unit configured to acquire a second position signal indicative of the position of a second element attached to an interventional device and placed on or within the object, wherein the first and second position signals are acquired synchronously over a given duration; and a third unit configured to calculate the relationship between the surface motion and the object motion based on the first and second position signals. The system includes a first sensing unit that obtains a first position signal representing the position of a first element located at the moving surface location of the body. outputs.L3:
The invention provides an apparatus for determining the relationship between motion at a surface of a body and motion of an object located within the body. The apparatus includes a first sensing unit configured to acquire a position signal from a first element positioned at a moving location on the body’s surface. A second sensing unit is configured to acquire a position signal from a second element attached to an interventional device and positioned on or within the internal object.

The first and second sensing units acquire their respective position signals synchronously over a specified period. Using these synchronized signals, a third unit calculates the relationship between the motion of the surface location and the motion of the internal object. The invention also provides a corresponding method for synchronously acquiring the position signals and determining the relationship between the surface motion and the motion of the object within the body.
outputs.L4:
An apparatus and method are provided for determining the relationship between motion at the surface of a subject’s body and motion of an internal anatomical object, such as an organ, tissue region, lesion, or other treatment target. The system uses a first tracking element positioned on or coupled to the body surface and a second tracking element attached to an interventional device located on, within, or adjacent to the internal object. The interventional device may include, for example, a catheter, needle, probe, guidewire, endoscope, biopsy instrument, or therapeutic applicator.

A tracking system measures the positions of the first and second tracking elements substantially simultaneously over a selected time interval. The resulting position signals represent body-surface movement and internal-object movement, respectively. Measurements may be obtained in one or more spatial dimensions and may include position, orientation, displacement, velocity, or other motion-related parameters. Synchronizing the measurements allows corresponding portions of the two signals to be compared, including movements caused by respiration, cardiac activity, patient shifting, or other physiological processes.

A processor analyzes the synchronized position signals to calculate a correlation or other mathematical relationship between surface motion and internal motion. The relationship may be expressed as a scaling factor, time delay, phase relationship, multidimensional transformation, regression model, or another predictive function. Signal filtering, artifact rejection, and compensation for tracking noise may be applied before or during the calculation. The relationship can also be updated periodically or continuously to account for changes in patient position, breathing pattern, instrument placement, or anatomical conditions.

Once the relationship has been established, subsequent movement of the internal object can be estimated from measurements of the surface-mounted element, even when direct tracking of the internal element is unavailable or undesirable. The estimated internal position may be displayed to an operator, supplied to an image-guidance or navigation system, or used to control the timing, positioning, or delivery of a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure. Confidence values or alerts may be generated when the measured surface motion no longer agrees sufficiently with the established relationship.

By correlating directly measured internal motion with readily observable body-surface motion, the apparatus provides a patient-specific motion model rather than relying solely on generalized assumptions about anatomical movement. This can improve motion monitoring and target localization during image-guided interventions, biopsies, ablation procedures, radiation delivery, surgery, and other procedures in which internal structures move relative to external reference points.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for an apparatus and method that determine the relationship between motion at a patient’s body surface and motion of an internal object using synchronously acquired position signals.
counterfactuals.output: An apparatus and method determine a relationship between motion at a patient’s body surface and motion of an internal object. A first position signal representing motion of one or more locations on the body surface and a second position signal representing motion of the internal object are acquired synchronously over a sampling interval. A processor temporally aligns the position signals and analyzes corresponding motion features to generate a correlation, transfer function, predictive model, or other mapping between external and internal motion. The relationship may account for time delay, direction, amplitude, periodicity, and nonrigid motion, and may be updated using subsequently acquired position data. Based on the determined relationship, motion or position of the internal object may be estimated from body-surface motion. The estimate may be used for patient monitoring, image acquisition or reconstruction, treatment planning, instrument navigation, or gated or dynamically adjusted delivery of therapy.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the following concept into formal patent language: synchronously measure the position of an external body marker and an internal marker on an interventional device, then calculate the relation between external surface motion and internal object motion.
counterfactuals.output:
**Exemplary Patent Claim Language**

1. A method for correlating external body motion with motion of an object within a subject, the method comprising:  
   - acquiring, by one or more tracking systems, a first plurality of position measurements of at least one external marker disposed on an external surface of the subject;  
   - acquiring a second plurality of position measurements of at least one internal marker associated with an interventional device positioned at least partially within the subject, wherein the first and second pluralities of position measurements are acquired substantially synchronously; and  
   - determining, by at least one processor, a spatial and/or temporal relationship between motion of the external surface and motion of the interventional device based on the first and second pluralities of position measurements.

2. The method of claim 1, wherein determining the relationship comprises generating a correlation model configured to estimate a position, orientation, displacement, velocity, or trajectory of the interventional device from measured motion of the external marker.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the first and second pluralities of position measurements are temporally registered using timestamps, a common clock, or synchronization signals.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein the relationship accounts for a phase delay, amplitude difference, nonlinear transformation, or hysteresis between the motion of the external surface and the motion of the interventional device.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Prepare a patent-style abstract for a medical motion-correlation system that links respiratory surface movement to the movement of an object within the body.
counterfactuals.output: A medical motion-correlation system is disclosed for estimating movement of an object within a patient based on respiratory movement of an external body surface. The system includes one or more sensors configured to acquire surface-position data during respiration, an imaging device configured to acquire positional data for the internal object, and a processor configured to temporally associate the surface-position data with the internal-object positional data. The processor generates a correlation model representing a relationship between respiratory surface movement and movement of the internal object and applies the model to subsequently acquired surface-position data to estimate a position, trajectory, or respiratory phase of the internal object. The correlation model may be updated in response to additional imaging data or a detected change in respiratory pattern. Estimated object motion may be provided to a medical imaging, diagnostic, surgical, or radiation-treatment system for motion compensation, gating, tracking, or treatment control.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an apparatus and corresponding method for determining how the motion of a location on a body’s surface relates to the motion of an internal object, using first and second position signals collected over the same time interval.
counterfactuals.output:
### Apparatus

An apparatus for determining the relationship between movement of a point on a patient’s body surface and movement of an internal object includes:

- a **first position-sensing system** configured to generate a first position signal representing the position of the surface location over a selected time interval;
- a **second position-sensing system** configured to generate a second position signal representing the position of the internal object over the same time interval;
- a **timing or synchronization mechanism** that time-aligns the first and second position signals; and
- a **processor** configured to compare the time-aligned signals and determine a motion relationship, such as a correlation function, transfer function, or mathematical model mapping surface motion to internal-object motion.

The apparatus may also include memory for storing the signals and model, and an output module for displaying or predicting the internal object’s position from subsequent surface-position measurements.

### Corresponding method

1. Monitor the position of a selected location on the body surface during a time interval to obtain a first position signal.
2. Monitor the position of an internal object during that same interval to obtain a second position signal.
3. Synchronize or time-align the two signals.
4. Compare the signals, optionally accounting for phase delay, hysteresis, periodicity, or other motion characteristics.
5. Determine and store a relationship between surface motion and internal-object motion.
6. Optionally apply the relationship to later measurements of the surface location to estimate, track, or predict the internal object’s position without continuously measuring it directly.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
